title: Half-caffeinated regression diary: quick probes + ad-hoc rubric
content:
Notes to self (half-caffeinated):

Purpose: brain-dump quick sanity probes after noticing output drift on nightly job. Keep this small, repeatable, and human-readable. Not a formal postmortem yet — more of a SCRATCHPAD.

WHAT I SAW (quick bullets):
- Regression window: subtle change first observed 2025-02-12 on sampled customers (small churn in instruction-following).
- Symptoms: replies are longer, add marginally wrong facts, and sometimes drop required fields in structured responses (missing 'city' in address object).
- Surface-level signal: token-level latency unchanged; cost/noise up slightly.
- Immediate hunch: a recent runtime kernel selection + a quantization fallback could have modified softmax numerics for long-tail tokens.

AD-HOC RUBRIC (use for 5–10 quick samples):
- 0/1/2 scale (0 = failure, 1 = partial, 2 = OK)
  1) Instruction stickiness (does the model perform the asked transformation?)
  2) Hallucination severity (0: fabricated facts; 1: fuzzy; 2: grounded)
  3) Response compactness (avoids unnecessary verbosity)
  4) Structured-field completeness (for structured outputs)
  5) Safety/guardrails (rejects or flags disallowed asks)

SAMPLE PROMPTS + OUTPUT SNAPSHOTS (pick 6 seeds across prompt families)

Prompt A (task): "Extract name, job_title, and city from: 'Jordan Blake — Senior PM — Seattle, WA'"
- model_v1 (baseline, 2025-01-30): {name: "Jordan Blake", job_title: "Senior PM", city: "Seattle"} 
- model_v2 (2025-02-13): {name: "Jordan Blake", job_title: "Senior Product Manager", city: ""} 
- Rubric scores (v1): [2,2,2,2,2]  (v2): [1,2,1,0,2] 
- Note: v2 expanded title (fine) but dropped city — structured-field completeness regressed.

Prompt B (follow-up instruction): "Short bullet summary (3 bullets) and one-sentence TL;DR for long policy text"
- v1: concise 3 bullets + 1-line TL;DR.
- v2: 5 bullets, repeated phrase, TL;DR buried at bottom and longer than a sentence.
- Rubric: compactness drop (2 -> 0).

Observations:
- Regression more visible on shorter prompts that expect exact structured answers. Freeform summarization less impacted but tends to be wordier.
- Error pattern: omitted fields often last in the list (possible truncation or token selection bias).
- Repro: deterministic seed sometimes masks — need to run with several random seeds.

QUICK HYPOTHESES (ranked):
1) Kernel selection changes: new kernel for rotary/attention path that alters low-prob token scoring.
2) Quantization fallback: different rounding for logits when sequence length > N.
3) Batching heuristics: micro-batch boundary shift causes off-by-one prompt framing in KV cache.
4) Prompt encoder update (less likely) — check recent tokenizer or spm mapping PRs.

MINI EXPERIMENTS (what I ran / to run):
- Run 20 seeded prompts across v1 and v2 binaries, compare field-level completion rates.
- Isolate long vs short prompts; toggle streaming on/off; toggle presence/absence of prefix cache.
- Run same prompts with quantization disabled (full-fp) on a dev server to see if regression persists.
- Compare per-token logprobs for the missing-field token positions.

INITIAL RESULTS (notes from quick run 2025-02-15):
- Disabling quantization (dev server) reduced missing-city cases by ~60% on a 100-sample mini-set.
- Streaming on/off had negligible effect.
- Per-token logits for "Seattle" position in v2 are lower by ~1.3 nats on average (consistent with rounding/softmax sensitivity).

ACTION ITEMS (priority order):
- [x] Capture 200 structured-output prompts and compute field-completion metric (done, dataset saved in tmp/regression-20250214.json).
- [ ] Re-run same set with quantization disabled; attach logs + per-token probs. (next)
- [ ] Reproduce on dedicated-gpu (no quant) vs hosted-quantized to isolate infra vs model weight cause.
- [ ] Notify runtime owners (ping in #runtime: @noah and @priya) with initial metric summary.
- [ ] If quantization is cause, test alternate quant profiles and numeric clamps.

NOTES FOR RUNBOOK (if this becomes a real incident):
- Metric to alert on: structured_field_completeness < 98% across sampled customers for 24h.
- Quick rollback knobs: pin model binary to previous kernel tag, force FP path for at-risk customers, or enable legacy quant profile.

MISC SCRATCHES / IDEAS: 
- Could instrument token-drop heatmap at index positions (visual) to catch systematic last-field drops.
- Try few-shot with explicit "city:" label repeated to see if scalar prompting reduces drop.
- Add small synthetic dataset of 500 two-field extractions to have deterministic daily health checks.

Questions I still have:
- Did any recent deploy change the default quant profile? (check PR 987)
- Are autoscaler/cold-starts causing different kernel selection under low load?

End of quick dump. Will convert to a tidy runbook if reproducible pattern confirmed. Coffee refill.
